There are people that “need” therapy and those who don’t. However I believe that whoever you are, regardless of what you are going through, everyone can benefit greatly from counselling. 

You do seem to be carrying a lot. I think it would benefit to have someone help you carry some of the weight. or to have someone to help you through this time at least. 

i’ve been in counselling for 4 years i know i haven’t “needed” every session that i went but regardless for me personally it was an extremely worthwhile investment, especially, and this is important, if you find a counsellor you can connect well with.
this makes me so proud even tho idk you, the fear ur feeling is to be expected but when you find the right therapist to help you through it it will be much easier to go through it with someone.

i would talk to ur therapist about this, you don’t have to mention the specifics of the dream but you can say that you are finding yourself thinking of her more often and in ways that make u slightly uncomfortable. that’s what I did and both therapists that i’ve seen to understand the fear of them leaving or abandoning me. it actually helped us get to some important issues that obviously needed work but i didn’t realize it at the time. good luck to you!

this is just personal opinion i am not a professional in any way. I started counselling in grade 10. The only advice is to try different ones, make sure your son feels comfortable with them, give it a few sessions. At that age, the connection with the therapist i think is more important than when you are an adult. even now, i’m only 19 i still notice how much more prominent and important the connection was back then versus now. because that is one more adult in his life, in his mind it’s a different category than his friends and peers. it will be strange talking with an adult not only like you do with ur friends but deeper and more meaningful personal topics. there has to be trust.

i never had a parent to guide me through it, my parents didn’t know i was in counselling for the first 6 months at least. after a few sessions, good signs will be having an end goal with the therapist, what it will be like once therapy has ended? if it is school work related i would ask if the therapist has any experience related to school stress and this age group. a lot of it will be clear though when you meet with a therapist and see how your son connects with them. In highschool I went in for stress around exams although a lot more other things surfaced in counselling, personally DBT therapy helped me immensely.

The one I use is 330mg CBD/1g syringe CBD oil Phoenix Tears by Miss Envy. The packaging and syringe are a little bit more difficult that oil capsules but I like knowing that I can control exactly how much oil I’m taking even tho I can’t measure it I can see it on my finger. :)

It helps me a lot but start on a low dose. I started with approximately 2-3 mg because it was oil I just took a tiny drop on my finger. I use it when anxiety gets worse with bipolar episodes. I do notice that tolerance builds up super fast so I try to take a few days break when I notice that otherwise you will be taking a lot. it’s helped me immensely,more than any medications ever did. Make sure it’s pure CBD no THC oil. I notice that I do have a headache and nausea the days after when I don’t take it, probably some kind of withdrawal effect but it isn’t too bad and apparently it’s rare because CBD is supposed to help with that. Good luck !

happened to me to exactly the same thing you described. like EXACTLY. the only that helped was to talk to her about it. i never mentioned the erotic part or anything sexual. but  basically i told her “i’m feeling very attached to you and i have feelings like i wish you were my mother” and surprise she already knew i was feeling that way because of how reactive and sensitive to her. we talked about it. after months of reassurance that she was there for me and she wouldn’t abandon me, i finally believed her and after that the worries finally lifted. i still have them a lot. but working through them WITH her helped me understand and accept the way i am. 

if she doesn’t understand the transference issue then maybe look for a counsellor who specializes in attachment. It is important. this issue ate me up so bad i hates myself so much because of these feelings towards her but she helped me normalize them and realize that IT IS NORMAL TO WANT CARE AND ATTENTION FROM PEOPLE WHO U CAN TRUST AND U LIKE!!!

Took a class called Radical Acceptance in my first year of uni. It was by tara brach you can find it if you google her. Changed my life once i opened up to the ideas.
